title: Minimum Cost to Buy Apples II
summary: Given an integer n and an array prices of n integers, and a 2D array roads with details of bidirectional roads, determine the minimum cost to buy apples at each shop.
statement: Given an integer n and an array prices of n integers, and a 2D array roads with details of bidirectional roads, determine the minimum cost to buy apples at each shop. For each shop, consider buying apples locally or traveling to another shop to buy apples, then returning with a cost multiplier applied. Return an array of minimum costs for each shop.
constraints: Travel empty pays cost; returning with apples pays cost×tax, and the two routes may differ.
For every starting shop, minimize outbound travel plus apple price plus loaded return travel.
hints: Outbound and loaded return travel define two different shortest-path metrics.
From each start, run Dijkstra once using cost and once using cost×tax.
For every buying shop j, combine empty distance, prices[j], and loaded distance, taking the minimum.
Shortest routes in the two phases are independent, so separately minimizing each phase for a fixed j is necessary and sufficient.
editorial: Shortest routes in the two phases are independent, so separately minimizing each phase for a fixed j is necessary and sufficient.

tests.explanation: From shop zero, buying at one costs 1+3+2=6; shop one buys locally for three.
Shop zero reaches shop two empty for one and returns for three, totaling five; local choices remain best for shops one and two.
